result.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens's sharing branch does `return response;` from a bare fetch, returning a raw Response, while the non-sharing branch returns the axios result. Zoho CRM code immediately does `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)`, which accesses `.data` — a raw fetch Response has no `.data` property, so this throws a TypeError when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: In sharing mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined and the guard `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError. Zoho CRM calendar operations crash with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' on the first token refresh whenever credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, returns a raw `fetch(...)` Response (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is assigned from `await refreshOAuthTokens(async () => await axios(...), "zohocrm", credential.userId);` and then immediately dereferenced as `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. If sharing mode is enabled and the sync endpoint is set, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` will be a Fetch `Response` (no `.data`), so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` will throw a TypeError. This matches the reported crash scenario on token refresh in sharing mode.
